title: The Basel Framework - Bank for International Settlements
summary: This is a comprehensive 1,982-page regulatory framework document from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) that consolidates all prudential standards for internationally active banks. The document covers capital definitions, risk-based capital requirements, credit risk approaches (standardized and IRB), market risk calculations, operational risk, and leverage ratios. No specific publication date is provided; this appears to be a living framework reference document downloaded in April 2026.
key_points: Contains comprehensive banking prudential standards including capital adequacy (CAP), risk-based capital (RBC), credit risk (CRE), market risk (MAR), operational risk (OPE), and leverage ratio (LEV) sections
Includes specific market risk framework (MAR10-MAR99) covering standardized approach and internal models approach for calculating capital requirements
Addresses counterparty credit risk definitions and capital treatment for central counterparties (CRE50-CRE56)
Covers cryptoasset exposures starting at SCO60
Includes provisions for systemically important bank buffers (RBC40) and global systemically important banks (SCO40)
Document has no explicit publication date; appears to be downloaded in April 2026 as a consolidated framework reference
why_it_matters: This framework establishes the foundational regulatory structure governing how banks calculate and maintain capital against market risk, credit risk, and operational risk. For market structure analysis, the market risk (MAR) sections directly impact how dealers size positions, provide liquidity, and manage risk - affecting bond spreads, derivatives pricing, and overall market depth. However, without a publication date, it is impossible to verify whether this version reflects current Basel III reforms or represents an earlier framework state.
macro_context: The Basel Framework is the primary global standard setter for banking prudential regulation. BCBS member jurisdictions have agreed to implement these standards for internationally active banks. The framework's periodic updates (including recent Basel III reforms) can materially affect bank balance sheets, risk appetite, and market-making capacity - with downstream effects on liquidity and spreads across fixed income and derivatives markets.
market_structure_context: This document is a regulatory reference framework. The MAR (market risk) section includes standardized approach provisions (MAR20-MAR23), internal models approach requirements (MAR30-MAR33), backtesting requirements, and P&L attribution tests. The CRE (credit risk) sections address counterparty credit risk calculations and capital treatment for central counterparties. These specifications influence dealer behavior, balance sheet usage, and market-making capacity. However, the lack of a publication date prevents verification of which framework version this represents.
